hero.headline: Fort Pierce could become rocket recovery hub for SpaceX and Blue Origin under new port plan
hero.body:
Fort Pierce is positioning itself to become a major recovery hub for commercial space launches, with an updated port plan that would accommodate rocket recovery operations for SpaceX and Blue Origin. The proposal would transform the local port into a key facility for retrieving rocket components after launches from Cape Canaveral.

The plan represents a significant economic development opportunity for Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County. The commercial space industry has grown rapidly along Florida's Space Coast, and recovery operations require specialized port facilities capable of handling large rocket boosters and other spacecraft components. Fort Pierce's location on the Atlantic coast makes it a strategic choice for companies looking to expand their recovery capabilities beyond existing facilities.

Both SpaceX and Blue Origin have increasingly focused on reusable rocket technology, which requires safe recovery and refurbishment of boosters and other expensive components after each launch. SpaceX currently recovers its Falcon 9 boosters on drone ships in the Atlantic, while Blue Origin is developing its New Glenn rocket with similar reusability goals. A dedicated recovery facility at Fort Pierce would provide these companies with additional capacity and flexibility for their operations.

The updated port plan is currently under review. If approved, the facility would need specialized infrastructure including reinforced docks, heavy-lift cranes, and secure storage areas for rocket hardware. The project could create jobs in maritime operations, logistics, and aerospace support services for the local community.

cards.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
cards.teaser: A 64-year-old man was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to force a 74-year-old woman into his vehicle at gunpoint in the parking lot of First United Methodist Church.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami, faces multiple felony charges following the attempted kidnapping at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard Sunday morning. The incident unfolded around 10:49 a.m. when Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder after setting fire to home with mother inside
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is facing attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was locked inside the room Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following the incident in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard, where officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the victim discovered smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and found Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly attacked her physically and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames before the victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door.

Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her, but she resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to receive treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for injuries sustained during the incident. Fire investigators from the Port St. Lucie Police Department, St. Lucie County Fire District, and the State Fire Marshal's Office determined the blaze was intentionally set.

Picard faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest without violence, with a total bond set at $510,000. The fire damaged the residence, prompting the American Red Cross to assist the victim with temporary housing and support services. Police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

cards.headline: School bus driver arrested in Florida after second student allegation
cards.body:
A Florida school bus driver has been arrested following a second allegation from a student. Law enforcement took action after receiving multiple reports concerning the driver's conduct with students.

The arrest represents the second complaint against the driver, prompting authorities to intervene. School transportation officials are working with law enforcement as the investigation continues.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about student safety during school transportation. Parents and school officials are reviewing protocols to ensure children remain protected while riding school buses.

School district administrators are expected to address transportation safety measures in response to the allegations. The investigation remains active as authorities work to determine the full scope of the incidents involving students.

cards.headline: Florida Legislature Sends DeSantis Property Tax Cut Plan to November Ballot
cards.body:
The Florida Legislature has approved Governor Ron DeSantis's property tax cut proposal, placing the measure on the November ballot for voters to decide. The legislative action came during a special session focused on tax relief, with both chambers passing the constitutional amendment that would allow Floridians statewide to vote on reducing property tax burdens.

The property tax cut plan represents a significant potential change to how local governments across Florida fund services. If approved by voters in November, the measure would alter the state's property tax structure. The proposal gained traction as property values and tax bills have risen across Florida in recent years, affecting homeowners and businesses throughout the state. DeSantis had made the tax cut a priority, calling on lawmakers to advance the measure.

Local government leaders in multiple Florida regions have voiced concerns about the proposal's impact on municipal budgets and services. Jacksonville-area officials expressed worries about how the tax reduction would affect their ability to fund essential services. The concerns reflect broader questions about whether local governments across the state will face budget shortfalls if voters approve the measure. Property taxes fund critical services including schools, police and fire departments, road maintenance, and other local infrastructure.

The measure now moves to Florida voters, who will make the final decision in the November election. Constitutional amendments in Florida require 60 percent voter approval to pass. The campaign period leading to November will likely feature debate over the balance between tax relief for Florida residents and maintaining funding for local services. Proponents argue the cut will provide meaningful relief to Floridians facing rising costs, while opponents warn of potential impacts on government services. The outcome will affect property taxpayers and local governments throughout the state.

cards.headline: Downtown Fort Pierce enforces parking limit with citations for stays over 2 hours
cards.teaser: Visitors to downtown Fort Pierce now face citations if they park for more than two hours, as the city enforces time limits on street parking.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce has begun issuing citations to drivers who exceed the two-hour parking limit in the downtown area. The enforcement affects visitors to businesses, restaurants, and other establishments along the city's main downtown streets.

The parking time limits are designed to encourage turnover and ensure that parking spaces remain available for multiple customers throughout the day. Business districts often implement such restrictions to balance the needs of shop owners who want consistent customer access against the limited number of available parking spaces. The citations represent a financial penalty for drivers who overstay the posted limit.

Downtown Fort Pierce has seen increased activity in recent years with new restaurants and retail establishments opening in the area. The parking enforcement is part of the city's broader effort to manage growth and maintain accessibility for visitors. Drivers planning extended visits to downtown Fort Pierce should be aware of the time restrictions and consider moving their vehicles or finding alternative parking options if they need to stay longer than two hours.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes annexation of Cresswind development
cards.teaser: The city of Sebastian has completed the annexation process for Cresswind, bringing the development into the city's jurisdiction.
cards.body:
Sebastian has finalized annexations related to the Cresswind development, officially bringing the property within city limits. The annexation represents an expansion of Sebastian's boundaries and adds new territory to the city's planning and service area.

Cresswind developments are typically active adult communities featuring homes designed for residents aged 55 and older. The annexation means Sebastian will now provide municipal services to the development and collect taxes from the properties. It also gives the city direct control over zoning, code enforcement, and development standards for the area.

Annexations affect both the city and existing residents. For Sebastian, the expanded boundaries mean additional tax revenue but also increased responsibility for services such as road maintenance, public safety, and infrastructure. The Cresswind residents will now participate in Sebastian city elections and receive city services rather than relying solely on county government. The finalization of this annexation completes a process that typically involves multiple readings and public hearings before city council.

cards.headline: Vero Beach approves $190,000 for new Iris Lane sidewalk
cards.teaser: The city of Vero Beach has approved spending $190,000 to construct a sidewalk along Iris Lane.
cards.body:
Vero Beach officials have approved a $190,000 project to build a sidewalk on Iris Lane. The investment in pedestrian infrastructure will provide a safe walking path along a street that currently lacks sidewalk facilities.

Sidewalk projects typically serve multiple purposes in residential areas, improving safety for pedestrians, schoolchildren, and residents who walk for exercise. Without sidewalks, pedestrians must walk in the street or on grass and dirt shoulders, creating potential conflicts with vehicle traffic. The Iris Lane project will add defined walking space separated from the roadway.

The $190,000 budget will cover design, materials, and construction of the sidewalk. Vero Beach, like many Florida communities, has worked to expand its network of pedestrian facilities as part of broader efforts to improve walkability and safety. The project joins other infrastructure improvements the city has undertaken to enhance the quality of life for residents and encourage more people to walk in their neighborhoods rather than rely exclusively on cars for short trips.

cards.headline: Vero Beach honors local woman with historical marker
cards.teaser: A Florida woman has been commemorated with a historical marker in Vero Beach, recognizing her contributions to the community.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has installed a historical marker honoring a Florida woman for her contributions to the area. The marker serves as a permanent recognition of her role in local history and provides residents and visitors with information about her significance to the community.

Historical markers are placed by communities to recognize important people, places, and events that shaped local development. They serve educational purposes and help preserve community memory for future generations. The markers typically include biographical information and explain why the person or site deserves recognition.

The installation of the marker in Vero Beach adds to the city's collection of historical sites and commemorations. These markers are often placed near locations significant to the person being honored, such as former residences, workplaces, or community facilities they helped establish. For residents of Vero Beach and Indian River County, the marker provides an opportunity to learn about local history and the individuals who contributed to building the community.

cards.headline: Former city councilmember Jewel Collins, known as 'Queen of Cocoa,' dies at 89
cards.teaser: Jewel Collins, a former city councilmember known as the 'Queen of Cocoa,' has died at age 89.
cards.body:
Jewel Collins, a former city councilmember who earned the title 'Queen of Cocoa,' died at the age of 89. Collins served in local government and became known for her community involvement and leadership.

Collins' nickname reflected her strong connection to her community and her influence in local affairs. During her time on the city council, she worked on issues affecting residents and participated in decisions shaping the city's development. Public officials who serve in local government often build lasting legacies through their work on issues ranging from infrastructure and public safety to economic development and community services.

The death of longtime public servants like Collins represents the loss of institutional knowledge and community connections built over decades. Many former council members remain active in their communities even after leaving office, continuing to advocate for local causes and mentor newer generations of civic leaders. Collins' passing at 89 marks the end of a life dedicated to public service and community engagement.

cards.headline: Florida county sees property value growth decline for fourth straight year
cards.teaser: A Florida county has experienced declining property value growth for four consecutive years, reflecting changes in the local real estate market.
cards.body:
Property value growth has declined for the fourth year in a row in a Florida county, continuing a trend that affects tax revenues and reflects broader real estate market conditions. The sustained slowdown marks a shift from the rapid appreciation that characterized Florida real estate in previous years.

Property values are a critical component of local government finance because they determine the tax base from which counties, cities, and school districts collect revenue. When property values grow more slowly or decline, governments face constraints on revenue even if tax rates remain unchanged. This can affect funding for schools, roads, public safety, and other services. Homeowners may see smaller increases in their property tax bills, but could also see reduced home equity growth.

The four-year trend suggests the county's real estate market has entered a different phase than the boom years that saw double-digit annual appreciation in many Florida markets. Factors affecting property values can include interest rates, insurance costs, local economic conditions, and broader housing market dynamics. For residents, slower growth in property values can be a mixed blessing, offering affordability benefits for new buyers while reducing wealth accumulation for existing homeowners.

cards.headline: Martin County Sheriff announces arrests in Operation Hammer Time theft ring that hit Stuart, Fort Pierce hardware stores
cards.teaser: Three men have been arrested in connection with a retail theft ring that burglarized more than 40 hardware stores across 13 counties, including locations in Stuart and Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in a retail theft ring dubbed Operation Hammer Time, which targeted hardware stores across Martin, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties from December 2025 to April 2026. Major Ruben Romero said Johnny Batista, 19, Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39, and Roberto Aldana-Ferrera, 31, were all involved in the series of burglaries that hit at least 40 stores across 13 counties. According to an affidavit from the Martin County Sheriff's Office, hardware stores in Stuart, Fort Pierce and Jupiter were among those targeted. Romero said roughly $500,000 worth of property was stolen, in addition to damage to stores, and the stolen goods were taken back to Miami-Dade County, where the suspects lived, to be sold.

The crews would use a sledgehammer or other blunt object to smash the glass and would often complete the thefts within minutes, before police arrived or alarms were triggered. Investigators say Batista is connected to the first known theft at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025. Aldana-Ferrera is in custody in Georgia, Batista was arrested in February for a vehicle theft and is in Martin County Jail, and Hernandez-Castro has a warrant out for his arrest. A fourth suspect, Maikell Fleitas, is deceased.

Romero emphasized the impact of these thefts on local residents, noting that inflation combined with retail theft drives up prices. "People can't go to work because they can't afford the tools," he said. The suspects are facing charges of racketeering, burglary over $1,000 in damage while masked, burglary of an occupied structure and burglary of an unoccupied structure. Romero said there are burglaries that happened previous to December, and investigators are still looking for one other suspect.

cards.headline: 5 hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash sparks fire on I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: Five people were injured Monday night after a multi-vehicle collision on Interstate 95 near Halpatiokee Regional Park that also sparked a vehicle fire.
cards.body:
The crash occurred just before 10 p.m. on I-95 northbound near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park in Stuart, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. When crews responded to the scene, they found one of the vehicles on fire and quickly extinguished the flames. Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment.

All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash. As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened. The Florida Highway Patrol is handling the investigation into the cause of the collision and fire.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood, wildlife officials monitoring
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before running toward nearby homes.
cards.body:
The video, posted on the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Facebook page, shows the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Bear Management Program said they are monitoring the bear. If it doesn't move from the area on its own, wildlife officials said their bear biologists may set a trap to try and capture and relocate it.

"As Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur," Port St. Lucie police stated on Facebook. "While seeing a bear may be surprising, it is not necessarily cause for alarm." According to the FWC, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents.

Wildlife officials recommend specific protocols when encountering black bears. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food and bird seed around their properties. During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route.

cards.headline: Former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces second charge as additional victim comes forward
cards.teaser: Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie, was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 after a second victim came forward with additional information for investigators.
cards.body:
Garcia, a former St. Lucie County school bus driver, now faces an additional charge in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children. The new arrest comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age. The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus.

During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The case was then referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at 772-462-7300 or email CrimeTips@stluciesheriff.gov.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home, late son's photos in lightning strike fire
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera was displaced last month after a lightning strike tore through her Fort Pierce home, destroying belongings including irreplaceable photos of her late son.
cards.body:
Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church last month when a utility worker stopped her outside. "When I go back home, I see, the utility guy tells me, hey I think your house is on fire," Rivera said. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire. Walking into her damaged home left her stunned. "I was in shock, I'm thinking that's just a dream, but no, it's reality," Rivera said.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son. "My son's pictures. My son passed away three years ago," Rivera said. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. "It's a lot that I'm dealing with. It's very, very overwhelming," Rivera said.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto one thing: gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out. "It's a blessing that I was not home," Rivera said. "And I was in a safe place instead of being at home to where something could've possibly happened to me." A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild.

hero.headline: Heiress donates land to Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve to prevent development
hero.body:
An heiress is buying up Florida land near Hobe Sound and donating it to conservation preserves to stop future development. The acquisitions directly benefit the Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve, a protected natural area in Martin County.

The land purchases and donations add acreage adjacent to the existing preserve, ensuring the environmentally sensitive scrub habitat remains undeveloped. The Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve protects one of Florida's rarest ecosystems, home to threatened species including the Florida scrub jay.

The donated parcels will expand the preserve's boundaries and create larger contiguous habitat blocks. By purchasing properties that might otherwise be developed for housing or commercial use, the heiress is permanently protecting the scrub ecosystem that makes Hobe Sound unique.

The land conservation effort comes as development pressure continues in Martin County, where natural areas face ongoing threats from residential and commercial projects. The donations ensure this particular stretch of scrubland will remain in its natural state for future generations.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes Cresswind annexations
cards.teaser: Sebastian has completed annexation proceedings for Cresswind properties, bringing new land into the city's boundaries.
cards.body:
The City of Sebastian has finalized annexations for the Cresswind development, officially bringing those properties under city jurisdiction. The annexations expand Sebastian's municipal boundaries to include the residential areas associated with the Cresswind community.

Annexation brings properties into city limits, subjecting them to Sebastian's municipal services, regulations, and tax structure. Residents in annexed areas typically receive city utilities, police and fire services, and other municipal benefits in exchange for city taxes and adherence to city codes.

The Cresswind annexations represent continued growth in Sebastian, an Indian River County city on the Atlantic coast. Annexation decisions require city council approval and follow specific legal procedures under Florida law.

cards.headline: Florida mall partially demolished, marking end of retail era
cards.teaser: A Florida shopping mall has been partly torn down, with photos documenting its earlier days when it served as a bustling retail center.
cards.body:
Demolition crews have partially demolished a Florida mall, marking the end of an era for a once-thriving shopping destination. Photos from the mall's heyday show the property when it was filled with shoppers and retail stores, a stark contrast to its current state.

The partial demolition reflects broader trends affecting traditional shopping malls across Florida and the nation. Many indoor malls have struggled as shopping habits shifted toward online retail and outdoor lifestyle centers, leaving older enclosed malls with declining occupancy and foot traffic.

The fate of the remaining portions of the mall property remains to be determined. Similar properties across Florida have been redeveloped into mixed-use projects, distribution centers, or entirely new residential and commercial developments.

cards.headline: Property value growth declines for fourth consecutive year in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has seen property value growth slow for four straight years, affecting tax revenues and local budgets.
cards.body:
Property value growth has declined for the fourth year in a row in a Florida county, representing a sustained slowdown in the real estate market. The consecutive years of declining growth rates signal a cooling trend after years of rapid appreciation.

Property values directly impact local government revenues, as counties, cities, and school districts rely heavily on property taxes to fund services. When property value growth slows, governments face pressure to either raise tax rates or cut budgets to maintain revenue levels.

The four-year trend suggests a longer-term shift in the county's real estate market rather than a temporary fluctuation. County officials and residents will watch future property appraisals closely, as continued slow growth could require adjustments to local government spending and tax rates.

cards.headline: New French cafe opens in Cocoa Beach
cards.teaser: Cocoa Beach has a new dining option with the opening of a French cafe bringing European-style cuisine to the Space Coast.
cards.body:
A new French cafe has opened its doors in Cocoa Beach, adding a European dining option to the beachside community. The restaurant brings French-style cuisine and cafe culture to Brevard County's Atlantic coast.

The cafe opening adds to Cocoa Beach's dining scene, which serves both local residents and tourists visiting the area's beaches and attractions. French cafes typically offer items like croissants, quiches, crepes, and espresso drinks alongside traditional breakfast and lunch fare.

New restaurant openings in Cocoa Beach contribute to the city's economy and provide variety for diners. The Space Coast community attracts visitors for its proximity to Kennedy Space Center, surfing beaches, and coastal atmosphere.

cards.headline: Heiress buys Florida land near Treasure Coast to block development
cards.teaser: An heiress is purchasing land in Florida to prevent it from being developed, protecting natural areas from future construction.
cards.body:
An heiress has been buying Florida land with the specific goal of stopping development and preserving natural areas. The land purchases focus on parcels that would otherwise be targets for residential or commercial construction.

The conservation-focused buying strategy protects environmentally sensitive lands from development pressure. As Florida continues to grow rapidly, undeveloped land faces constant pressure from builders and developers looking to create new housing, shopping centers, and other projects.

By purchasing land outright, the heiress can control its future use and ensure it remains undeveloped. Many conservation buyers donate purchased land to preservation organizations or place conservation easements on properties to permanently protect them from development.

A new restaurant is coming to a bustling area of Lexington, though the business is not local to the Treasure Coast. The establishment will join other dining and retail options in an active commercial district.

Restaurant openings reflect confidence in local economic conditions and consumer spending. Successful restaurant corridors attract multiple concepts as operators seek locations with proven customer traffic and demographics.

The new restaurant will need to compete with existing establishments in the area while also benefiting from the foot traffic and visibility that comes with a busy commercial location. Restaurant industry success rates improve in proven dining districts compared to standalone locations.

hero.headline: School bus driver arrested in Florida after second student allegation
hero.body:
A Florida school bus driver has been arrested following a second allegation from a student. Law enforcement took action after receiving multiple reports concerning the driver's conduct with students.

The arrest represents the second complaint against the driver, prompting authorities to intervene. School transportation officials are working with law enforcement as the investigation continues.

School district administrators are expected to address transportation safety measures in response to the allegations. The investigation remains active as authorities work to determine the full scope of the incidents involving students.

cards.headline: Property value growth declines for fourth straight year in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has seen property value growth slow for four consecutive years, a trend that could affect local budgets and tax revenues.
cards.body:
Property values in a Florida county have shown declining growth rates for the fourth year in a row. The continued slowdown marks a significant shift in the local real estate market after years of rapid appreciation.

The decline in property value growth has implications for county budgets, school funding, and local government services that rely on property tax revenues. Local officials are monitoring the trend as they plan future budgets and assess revenue projections.

While property values are still growing, the slower rate of increase represents a change from the robust growth seen in earlier years. Homeowners and local governments alike are adjusting to the new market conditions as the county's real estate sector stabilizes.

cards.headline: Four-vehicle crash shuts down northbound I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: A multi-vehicle collision closed northbound lanes of Interstate 95 in Martin County, causing major traffic disruptions.

Drivers faced significant delays as crews worked to clear the wreckage and investigate the crash. The closure affected one of the main traffic arteries through Martin County during a busy travel period.

Authorities worked to reopen the interstate as quickly as possible while ensuring the safety of motorists and emergency personnel. The crash serves as a reminder of the importance of safe driving practices on the busy corridor that runs through Martin County.

cards.headline: Florida lawmakers debate property tax proposal affecting local services
cards.teaser: State legislators are considering changes to property tax policy that could impact funding for schools, police, and other local services across Florida.

Florida lawmakers are debating a property tax proposal that has raised concerns among local government officials about its potential impact on essential services. The discussion centers on how changes to property tax policy would affect funding for schools, law enforcement, fire departments, and other locally funded services.

Local officials have expressed concern that reducing property tax revenues could force difficult budget decisions affecting services residents depend on. The debate highlights the tension between tax relief for property owners and maintaining adequate funding for local governments.

As the proposal moves through the legislative process, Treasure Coast communities are watching closely to see how any changes might affect their ability to fund schools, public safety, and infrastructure projects. The outcome could have lasting effects on local budgets and service levels throughout the region.

cards.headline: State legislature approves expanded homestead exemption for constitutional ballot
cards.teaser: Florida lawmakers have approved placing a constitutional amendment on the ballot that would expand the homestead property tax exemption for residents.
cards.body:
The Florida legislature has approved a measure to place a constitutional amendment on the ballot that would expand the homestead property tax exemption. Voters will have the opportunity to decide whether to increase the exemption amount, which would reduce property tax bills for homeowners who claim their primary residence.

The proposed amendment represents a potential tax break for Florida homeowners, but local governments are concerned about the impact on revenues used to fund schools, emergency services, and infrastructure. The homestead exemption removes a portion of a home's assessed value from taxation, and expanding it would further reduce the taxable base.

Treasure Coast residents will see the amendment on an upcoming ballot, giving them direct say over property tax policy. The measure's passage or failure will affect household budgets and local government finances throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

cards.headline: Miami-Dade and Broward schools end this week across Florida
cards.teaser: School districts in Miami-Dade and Broward counties wrap up the academic year this week, marking the end of classes for thousands of students.
cards.body:
The school year comes to a close this week for students in Miami-Dade and Broward counties as part of Florida's varied school calendar system. The end of classes marks the beginning of summer break for students across South Florida's largest school districts.

Florida school districts operate on different calendars, with some communities starting and ending the school year at different times. The varied schedules reflect local preferences and needs as districts balance instructional time with breaks throughout the year.

As South Florida students finish their school year, districts across the state continue to follow their own calendars. Treasure Coast school districts operate on their own schedules, with end dates determined by local school boards based on community needs and state requirements.

The Florida Trust for Historic Preservation has revealed its 2026 list of 11 endangered historic sites across the state. The list serves to draw attention to historic buildings and sites that need preservation efforts, funding, or policy changes to survive. Properties on the list range from historic structures to cultural landscapes that tell the story of Florida's past.

Historic preservation advocates use the annual list to rally support for endangered sites and encourage communities to protect their architectural heritage. The designation often helps generate interest in saving threatened properties before they are lost to future generations.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie to Gain Professional Soccer Team in USL League One

Port St. Lucie is gaining a professional soccer team as part of USL League One's expansion plans. The city will join Fort Lauderdale in welcoming teams to the third-tier professional soccer league, marking a significant addition to the Treasure Coast sports landscape.

The addition of a Port St. Lucie franchise will bring regular professional sporting events to St. Lucie County, offering residents the opportunity to support a local professional team.

The expansion reflects growing interest in soccer across Florida and represents a notable investment in Port St. Lucie's sports infrastructure. The timing of the team's first season and additional details about stadium arrangements and team branding will be announced as the expansion plans move forward. The Junior Lifeguard Camp is opening for its first two weeks of summer programming on the Treasure Coast, offering young residents hands-on training in water safety and beach rescue skills. The Artemis II mission represents the first crewed voyage to the Moon in over 50 years, drawing space enthusiasts and curious travelers from around the world to launch viewing areas along Florida's east coast. Brevard County, home to Kennedy Space Center, serves as the epicenter for the event, though overflow crowds may reach as far south as the Treasure Coast.

Local businesses in Sebastian and Vero Beach, the northernmost communities in Indian River County, may see spillover traffic from the launch as visitors seek accommodations and services. The economic impact of major space launches extends beyond Brevard County, benefiting restaurants, gas stations, and shops throughout the region as travelers pass through on their way to viewing locations.

Students attending the camp come from Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach, and Riviera Beach. Each participant assembles a computer from donated parts and takes it home at the end of the program, addressing technology access gaps for children who might not otherwise have a personal computer. The curriculum also includes fundamental AI concepts, preparing young learners for a technology-driven future.

The peer-led teaching model empowers children to share knowledge with one another, building confidence in both instructors and students. Parent volunteers and The Weiss School provide support for the program, which uses community donations to keep costs down and maintain its free enrollment. Organizers hope the model will inspire similar student-led technology programs across Palm Beach County and beyond.

hero.headline: Florida Legislature Sends DeSantis Property Tax Cut Plan to November Ballot
hero.body:
The Florida Legislature has approved Governor Ron DeSantis's property tax cut proposal, placing the measure on the November ballot for voters to decide. The legislative action came during a special session focused on tax relief, with both chambers passing the constitutional amendment that would allow Floridians statewide to vote on reducing property tax burdens.

The property tax cut plan represents a significant potential change to how local governments across Florida fund services. If approved by voters in November, the measure would alter the state's property tax structure. The proposal gained traction as property values and tax bills have risen across Florida in recent years, affecting homeowners and businesses throughout the state. DeSantis had made the tax cut a priority, calling on lawmakers to advance the measure.

Local government leaders in multiple Florida regions have voiced concerns about the proposal's impact on municipal budgets and services. Jacksonville-area officials expressed worries about how the tax reduction would affect their ability to fund essential services. The concerns reflect broader questions about whether local governments across the state will face budget shortfalls if voters approve the measure. Property taxes fund critical services including schools, police and fire departments, road maintenance, and other local infrastructure.

The measure now moves to Florida voters, who will make the final decision in the November election. Constitutional amendments in Florida require 60 percent voter approval to pass. The campaign period leading to November will likely feature debate over the balance between tax relief for Florida residents and maintaining funding for local services. Proponents argue the cut will provide meaningful relief to Floridians facing rising costs, while opponents warn of potential impacts on government services. The outcome will affect property taxpayers and local governments throughout the state.

The case involved the death of the infant while she was in the care of her mother's boyfriend. The crime and subsequent conviction led to a death sentence that was carried out after years of legal proceedings through Florida's court system.

The execution adds to the ongoing debate about capital punishment in Florida. The state maintains the death penalty and conducts executions for those convicted of the most serious crimes. This case involved the murder of a particularly vulnerable victim, an infant who died at the hands of someone entrusted with her care.

Central Florida residents should monitor weather conditions and be prepared for rapid changes. The severe weather threat affects a populated region of the state that includes the Orlando metropolitan area and surrounding communities. Forecasters will continue tracking the front's progress and intensity as it moves through.

The extremely short timeframe between the attendant entering the booth and being struck highlights the sudden nature of the accident. Beach toll booth attendants collect fees from visitors accessing certain Florida beaches, a job that involves interaction with vehicle traffic.

The incident remains under investigation by the Volusia County Sheriff's Office. The beach worker's condition and the circumstances leading to the truck striking the booth area are part of the ongoing inquiry into what happened.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff arrests three in retail theft ring that hit Stuart and 40+ hardware stores across Florida
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in a multi-county retail theft operation dubbed Operation Hammer Time. Major Ruben Romero said Johnny Batista, 19, Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39, and Roberto Aldana-Ferrera, 31, were involved in a series of burglaries at hardware stores across Martin, Palm Beach, and St. Lucie counties from December 2025 to April 2026. At least 40 stores across 13 counties were burglarized, including hardware stores in Stuart, Fort Pierce, Jupiter, Lake Worth, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, and West Palm Beach, as well as stores in Broward County.

Investigators say the theft ring stole roughly $500,000 worth of property and caused additional damage to stores. The crews would use a sledgehammer or other blunt object to smash the glass and often complete the thefts within minutes, before police arrived or alarms were triggered. The stolen goods were taken back to Miami-Dade County, where the suspects lived, to be sold. Batista is connected to the first known theft at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025.

Romero explained the wider community impact of these crimes. "There's already inflation that we notice severely in our state, and the more they steal, the more damage they cause, the more expensive things are," he said. "People can't go to work because they can't afford the tools." A fourth suspect, Maikell Fleitas, is deceased.

Batista was arrested in February for a vehicle theft and is in Martin County Jail. Aldana-Ferrera is in custody in Georgia, and Hernandez-Castro has a warrant out for his arrest. Romero said there are burglaries that happened previous to December, and investigators are still looking for one other suspect. The suspects are facing charges of racketeering, burglary over $1,000 in damage while masked, burglary of an occupied structure, and burglary of an unoccupied structure.

cards.headline: Five hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash sparks fire on I-95 in Martin County

The collision occurred just before 10 p.m. on I-95 northbound near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene, where they found one of the vehicles on fire. Crews quickly extinguished the flames.

Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment. All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash.

As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened. The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash.

Conservation efforts in Martin County have focused on protecting natural areas from development pressure as the Treasure Coast continues to grow. The donation represents a significant addition to protected lands in the Hobe Sound area.

cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office held a news conference Tuesday to provide details on Operation Hammertime, an investigation into a retail theft ring that targeted hardware stores across Florida. Major Ruben Romero outlined the scope of the burglaries and the arrests that have been made.

The operation involved coordination between multiple law enforcement agencies as investigators tracked the suspects who were hitting stores across 13 counties. The Sheriff's Office detailed how the crew operated and the significant financial impact on businesses and communities.

The news conference provided an opportunity for the Sheriff's Office to explain the investigation and warn other retailers about similar theft operations. Law enforcement officials emphasized the ongoing nature of the investigation and their continued search for additional suspects.

hero.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church, witnesses intervene
hero.teaser: A North Miami man was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a Port St. Lucie church parking lot, with Good Samaritans intervening to stop the attack.
hero.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami, faces multiple felony charges following the incident at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard Sunday morning. The attempted kidnapping unfolded around 10:49 a.m. in the church parking lot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her.

Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood, officials monitoring
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before running toward nearby homes, marking an unusual wildlife sighting along the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie Police Department posted the video on their Facebook page showing the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Bear Management Program said they are monitoring the bear. If it does not move from the area on its own, bear biologists may set a trap to try and capture and relocate it.

Port St. Lucie police stated that as Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur. While seeing a bear may be surprising, officials said it is not necessarily cause for alarm. According to the FWC, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents.

Wildlife officials emphasize specific protocols when encountering black bears in residential areas. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food, and bird seed around their properties. During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route.

cards.headline: Former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces new charges as second victim comes forward
cards.teaser: A former St. Lucie County school bus driver is facing an additional charge after a second victim came forward in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children.
cards.body:
Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie, was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when a second victim came forward with additional information for investigators. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The case was then referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at (772) 462-7300 or email CrimeTips@stluciesheriff.gov.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home, irreplaceable belongings after lightning strike destroys residence
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and seeking help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church last month when a utility worker stopped her outside. When she arrived, the utility worker told her he thought her house was on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire. Walking into her damaged home left her stunned.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out. A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild.

cards.headline: Historic Boston House in downtown Fort Pierce reopens as new dining destination
cards.teaser: The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce landmark for more than a century, has officially reopened as a new dining experience, bringing fresh energy to the city's downtown revitalization efforts.
cards.body:
Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades. Now, its newest owners are working to preserve its past while reimagining its purpose. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said the goal is simple: make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy. Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development.

During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past. General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader momentum downtown. Fort Pierce has had a reputation, and they really have done a great job bringing new life to the downtown area, Laird said.

Each room in the Boston House offers a distinct experience rooted in local history, blending preservation with a modern dining atmosphere. Angelos said the goal is keeping the authenticity intact while also bringing a new breath of fresh air into the town. The Boston House now stands as both a historic landmark and a renewed gathering place serving up a new chapter for downtown Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District honors fallen firefighter Connor Whitehead
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District held a ceremony to honor firefighter Connor Whitehead following his death.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District honored firefighter Connor Whitehead after his death, recognizing his service to the community. The ceremony brought together members of the fire district and the local community to pay tribute to Whitehead's dedication and sacrifice as a first responder.

The memorial service reflects the close bonds within St. Lucie County's emergency services community and the impact Whitehead had on his colleagues and the residents he served. Fire district personnel gathered to remember Whitehead's commitment to protecting the community and his contributions to the department.

The loss of a firefighter affects not only the fire district but the entire Treasure Coast community, reminding residents of the risks first responders face daily while serving and protecting their neighbors.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder charges after allegedly setting fire to bedroom with person inside
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is in custody facing attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, is being held on $510,000 bond following the incident in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

Port St. Lucie police responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m. Sunday. Officers arrived to find flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely. The investigation revealed that the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to receive treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for treatment of injuries sustained during the incident.

Multiple agencies responded to investigate the incident, including the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Criminal Investigations Division, Crime Scene Investigators, St. Lucie County Fire District, and the State Fire Marshal's Office. Fire investigators determined the blaze was intentionally set. The fire damaged the residence, prompting the American Red Cross to assist the victim with temporary housing and support services. Picard was taken to a hospital for medical evaluation before being cleared and transported to jail. She faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest without violence. Police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community.

hero.headline: Body found of suspect who killed wife and another man at Vero Beach library
hero.body:
Law enforcement recovered the body of a suspect who killed his wife and another man at a Vero Beach library before escaping into the ocean. The suspect had fled into the water following the double homicide at the library.

The incident occurred at a Vero Beach library where two people were killed in the attack. After the killings, the suspect escaped by going into the ocean, prompting a search by authorities.

The case involved a domestic situation that turned deadly when the suspect targeted his wife and another man at the public facility. The library became the scene of a violent crime that shocked the Vero Beach community.

Authorities conducted a search for the suspect after he entered the ocean. The recovery of his body brings closure to the manhunt that followed the deadly attack at the library facility.

cards.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway with Macy's anchor store coming down
cards.teaser: Demolition has begun at Indian River Mall with crews tearing down the former Macy's anchor store as part of a transformation project.
cards.body:
Demolition work is underway at Indian River Mall as crews dismantle the former Macy's anchor store. The partial demolition marks the beginning of changes to the shopping center that has served the community for decades.

The mall demolition represents a transformation for the property as developers prepare to reimagine the site. Photos from the mall's heyday show the facility during its peak years when it served as a central shopping destination for Indian River County residents.

The project will reshape the mall property into a new development. Plans show what the site could look like after demolition is complete, signaling a new chapter for the location that has been a familiar landmark in the area.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes Cresswind annexations
cards.teaser: The City of Sebastian has completed annexations related to the Cresswind development.
cards.body:
Sebastian city officials have finalized annexation proceedings for properties associated with the Cresswind development. The annexations bring additional land into the city limits as part of the ongoing development project.

The Cresswind project represents growth for Sebastian as new residential areas are incorporated into the city. The annexation process involved formal approval by city officials to expand the municipal boundaries.

The completed annexations will allow the development to move forward under Sebastian's jurisdiction. The Cresswind project is expected to bring new housing to the area as the city continues to manage growth and development within its expanding borders.

cards.headline: Indian River County Racquet Club request continues before commissioners
cards.teaser: Indian River County commissioners are continuing to review a request related to the Racquet Club property.
cards.body:
County commissioners in Indian River County are continuing deliberations on a request involving the Racquet Club. The matter remains under review as officials consider the proposal before them.

The Racquet Club request has been brought before the county commission for consideration. The ongoing review process involves county officials evaluating the proposal and its potential impacts on the community.

Commissioners will continue examining the Racquet Club matter in upcoming meetings. The decision on the request will affect the future of the property and its use within Indian River County.

cards.headline: WWII veteran Bill Keegan celebrates 102nd birthday in Indian River County
cards.teaser: World War II veteran Bill Keegan marked his 102nd birthday in Indian River County.
cards.body:
Bill Keegan, a World War II veteran living in Indian River County, celebrated his 102nd birthday this week. The milestone birthday honors a man who served his country during the Second World War and has lived more than a century.

Keegan's birthday celebration recognizes not only his long life but also his service during World War II. Veterans like Keegan represent a dwindling generation of Americans who fought in the global conflict that shaped the modern world.

The centenarian's birthday in Indian River County highlights the presence of veterans from the Greatest Generation still living in local communities. Keegan's longevity and continued presence serve as a living connection to a pivotal period in American history.

cards.headline: Woman found floating in Indian River Lagoon identified
cards.teaser: Authorities have identified a woman whose body was found floating in the Indian River Lagoon in Florida.
cards.body:
Law enforcement officials have identified a woman who was discovered floating in the Indian River Lagoon. The discovery prompted an investigation by authorities working to determine the circumstances surrounding her death.

The woman's body was found in the lagoon, a waterway that runs along Florida's east coast through multiple counties. Investigators worked to identify the victim and notify family members.

The identification of the woman marks a step forward in the investigation. Authorities continue examining the circumstances that led to her being found in the Indian River Lagoon.

cards.headline: Florida woman honored with historical marker in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A historical marker has been installed in Vero Beach to commemorate a Florida woman's contributions.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has installed a historical marker to honor a Florida woman who made significant contributions to the area. The marker serves as a permanent recognition of her legacy and impact on the community.

The commemorative marker in Vero Beach ensures that future generations will learn about the woman's role in local history. Historical markers like this one preserve important stories and recognize individuals who shaped their communities.

The installation of the marker represents the community's commitment to preserving and honoring local history. Vero Beach residents and visitors can now learn about the woman's achievements through the historical marker placed in her honor.
